source_text: Non volentis neque currentis sed miserentis Dei. Cuius vult miseretur, et quem vult indurat. Gloria Deo. Amen.
orientation: Origen is closing his commentary on Romans by quoting Paul's words about God's mercy and hardening.
pass_a_gloss: Not of the one willing nor of the one running but of God having mercy. Whom he wills he has mercy on, and whom he wills he hardens. Glory to God. Amen.

choices.term: Non volentis neque currentis sed miserentis Dei
choices.english: Not of the one willing nor of the one running but of God having mercy
choices.why: Keeps the genitive participles as agents and preserves the contrast between human effort and divine mercy
rejected: It does not depend on human will or effort but on God's mercy
Not of him who wills nor of him who runs but of God who shows mercy

choices.term: Cuius vult miseretur, et quem vult indurat
choices.english: Whom he wills he has mercy on, and whom he wills he hardens
choices.why: Preserves the parallel structure and the active divine agency in both mercy and hardening
rejected: He has mercy on whomever he wills, and he hardens whomever he wills
On whom he wills he has mercy, and whom he wills he hardens

choices.why: Standard doxological formula; dative Deo rendered as 'to God'

pass_b_english: It does not depend on the one who wills or the one who runs, but on God who has mercy (Romans 9:16). He has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills (Romans 9:18). Glory to God. Amen.
